lyrics:
[Intro: music-box piano, hard kick and snare, kids laughing]

[Hook: children's choir, bright and loud]
We don't get no snow days
Daddy goes in anyway
Boots by the door at four a.m.
Somebody's gotta clear the way
No snow days, no snow days
He goes in anyway

[Verse 1: male rap, rough and proud]
Radio says school's out, hear 'em cheering down the hall
I'm already in the truck, I got the call
Twelve on, twelve off, then twelve again
Salt in my beard and a thermos for a friend
My old man drove a bus through every storm they named
I didn't get it then. I get it now. Same.
You never see my face, you just see the road is black
That's the job. You wake up and I've been there and back.

[Hook: children's choir, bright and loud]
We don't get no snow days
Daddy goes in anyway
Boots by the door at four a.m.
Somebody's gotta clear the way
No snow days, no snow days
He goes in anyway

[Verse 2: rap, warmer, strings in]
Missed a recital, missed a game, I missed a tooth
I ain't gonna dress that up. That's just the truth.
But the lights are on, there's cereal, the heat stays warm
And every kid on this route gets to school after the storm
My daughter drew a picture, me, a cape, a plow
Stuck it on the dash. I'm looking at it now.
Come spring I'm taking Fridays. That's a vow I'm gonna keep.
Tonight I got the hill by the hospital. Go to sleep.

[Bridge: kids alone, clapping game rhythm]
Nurses! (No snow days)
Drivers! (No snow days)
Linemen! (No snow days)
My dad! (No snow days)

[Final Hook: children's choir, brass, drums loudest]
We don't get no snow days
Daddy goes in anyway
Boots by the door at four a.m.
Somebody's gotta clear the way
No snow days, no snow days
He goes in anyway

[Outro: plough blade scraping, a door, small voice: "He's home!"]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 90 BPM, 4/4, A minor. Hard-hitting and bouncing, tough and sweet at once.

VOICE: The rapper is a working man in his forties, rough-voiced, plain and proud, with a Northeastern edge. The hook is sung by a choir of eight to ten children, loud, bright and slightly ragged, like a school assembly. They shout the bridge as a call and response.

INSTRUMENTS: A music-box-style piano figure, a hard, dry kick and snare, a heavy bass, strings from verse 2, a brass section in the final hook, handclaps, a plough blade and winter sounds.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano and beat. 0:12 Hook 1. 0:38 Verse 1. 1:22 Hook 2. 1:48 Verse 2. 2:32 Bridge, kids. 2:48 Final hook. 3:14 Outro, plough, door and a child's voice at 3:34.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-1990s New York rap: drums hard and loud, the children's voices bright on top, everything dry and punchy.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'Stuck it on the dash. I'm looking at it now.' at 2:16.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original tells of escaping a hard life. This is about a man who stayed in one, on purpose, so that a town's children could get to school.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Tired, proud, honest about the cost, home.
